clues.text: Israel named this wilderness food, which was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
In the wilderness, Israelites ground it on handmills, boiled it in pots, or shaped it into cakes.
It stopped for Israel at Gilgal, near Jericho, the day after they ate the produce of Canaan.
Moses said God gave it to hungry Israel so they would learn that people do not live on bread alone.
In the Capernaum synagogue, Jesus said the fathers ate it in the wilderness and still died.
Inside the ark of the covenant sat a gold jar of it, beside Aaron's staff that had budded.
In the wilderness, God gave Israel two days' worth of it on the sixth day so they could rest on the Sabbath.
